What are the $y$-intercepts of the parabola shown above?

feedback.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14096769/assets/f164da846baf0488c472fbda94d10026247a6b9b613cc68d33d4ec43a5632d53.png)

**From top to bottom**, the **exact** values of the $y$-intercepts of the parabola shown above are{{field-1}}
and
{{field-2}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the equation of the parabola. From the diagram, we see that the parabola has a vertex at $(1,-1)$ and passes through the point $(-1,-3).$

The general standard equation of a left- or right-opening parabola with vertex at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
(y-k)^{2}=4p(x-h),
$$

and substituting $(h,k)=(1,-1)$ into the above gives

$$
(y+1)^{2}=4p(x-1).
$$

Now, we need to find $p.$ Since the parabola passes through the point $(-1,-3),$ we substitute $x=-1$ and $y=-3$ into the equation and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(-3+1)^{2} & =4p(-1-1) \\ 4 & =4p(-2) \\ p & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the parabola is

$$
\begin{aligned}(y+1)^{2} & =-2(x-1).\end{aligned}
$$

When the parabola intersects the $y$-axis, we must have $x=0.$ So, we substitute $x=0$ into the equation of the parabola and solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(y+1)^{2} & =-2(0-1) \\ (y+1)^{2} & =2 \\ y+1 & =\pm \sqrt{2} \\ y & =\pm \sqrt{2}-1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, from top to bottom, the $y$-intercepts are $\sqrt{2}-1$ and  $-\sqrt{2}-1.$
